name: Kaiming Liu
title: Physics PhD student
description: Kaiming Liu is a Physics PhD student at UIUC studying probabilistic machine learning and robust prediction in scientific inverse problems.
bio: My research focuses on probabilistic machine learning for inverse problems, where one measurement can have several plausible explanations.
I model these alternatives and study how predictions change from simulations to real measurements.
background: In Vidya Madhavan’s group at UIUC, I grew thin films with molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and studied electronic structure with STM/STS in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV). I developed automation and Python/MATLAB analysis tools. That experience informs how I test models against real measurements.
interests: Probabilistic machine learning; conditional density modeling; non-unique inverse problems; robustness under distribution shift; simulation-to-experiment transfer; neural many-body models.

education.degree: Special Class for the Gifted Young

experience.role: Graduate researcher, Bryan K. Clark group

projects.title: Conditional density modeling / crystal-field parameters
bullets: Built residual-MLP conditional Gaussian mixtures for conditional density estimation from magnetic susceptibility.
Represented multiple plausible solutions and checked them by reconstructing susceptibility; studied robustness on simulated and experimental data.
Evaluated conditional Gaussian mixtures and conditional RealNVP normalizing flows in a pilot density-model comparison.

projects.title: Robust inverse prediction / neutron scattering
bullets: Trained MLP and ResNet conditional Gaussian mixtures to infer exchange parameters from high-dimensional neutron-scattering maps.
Checked predictions with Sunny forward simulations and classical fit references; tested noise, intensity scaling, and background offsets.

projects.title: Neural-network backflow / JAX and Monte Carlo
bullets: Implemented neural-network backflow and variational Monte Carlo in JAX for Hubbard models, with GPU/multi-GPU sampling.
Profiled local-energy evaluation and gradient synchronization; verified chunked evaluation and global reductions against reference computations.
Grew thin-film heterostructures with MBE and characterized electronic structure with STM/STS in ultrahigh vacuum.
Automated growth temperature control and built Python/MATLAB tools for quasiparticle-interference analysis.
Simulated Rydberg-atom dynamics and photon-mediated interactions in Python/MATLAB to study quantum nonlinear optics.
Built a discrete-time lattice model of two-qubit phase-flip dynamics and many-body regimes.

experience.role: Research assistant, Michael F. Crommie group
bullets: Assisted synthesis and STM characterization of graphene nanoribbons with five-membered rings to study their electronic states.

teaching.text: Led discussion and laboratory sections, held office hours, and provided feedback on assignments in electromagnetism and modern physics.

researchProfile: Machine learning for probabilistic inference and robust prediction in scientific inverse problems with multiple plausible solutions.
